signals.name: Silver
signals.label: Holds its bid THROUGH the Iran de-escalation (~$58.5) — the structural-bull tell as the war premium unwinds
signals.detail: Silver opened ~$58.3-58.6 Mon 3 Aug (recovering Fri's ~$57.7 hot-PCE dip); gold back above ~$4,050 (Dec futures ~$4,135); 10Y eased to ~4.7%; DXY ~99.9. Levels as of the Mon 3 Aug US close
signals.takeaway: The book's single most important line item firmed even as oil crashed and the safe-haven war premium bled out — the clearest sign this is a structural-deficit/inflation-hedge bull (Silver Institute's 6th straight annual deficit), not just a geopolitical fear trade. The two-way risk is a still-firm dollar and any hot inflation print; with the oil shock relieved and labor softening, the near-term balance tilts back toward the metals. Favor gold-heavy GDX over pure silver leverage into Friday's 7 Aug jobs report.

signals.name: Crude oil / Energy
signals.label: Crashes ~5-7% as Trump calls off Iran strikes and a Hormuz-reopening deal turns 'imminent'
signals.detail: WTI fell from ~$86 toward ~$79-82 (Brent lower) on 3 Aug after Trump paused the threatened weekend strikes and said talks began Monday; a Hormuz-reopening deal is described as 'imminent' (Iran confirms talks)
signals.takeaway: The dominant cross-portfolio driver FLIPPED back to de-escalation: oil crashed, unwinding the inflation/rate-hike premium that had pressured the rate-sensitive core (levered silver, S-REITs, HK tech) — a net relief for the book even as it pressures the small energy long and trims the safe-haven bid. The catch: the deal is not signed. A talks collapse snaps oil and the safe-haven bid straight back, so keep gold-heavy GDX as the two-way hedge rather than chasing.

signals.name: Alphabet
signals.label: Whale magnet — Berkshire's new ~$16.6B stake plus Soros/Tepper/Tiger/Bridgewater all hold
signals.detail: Berkshire near-tripled GOOGL to ~57.8M shares (~$16.6B) in Q1; also held by Soros, Tepper, Tiger Global and Bridgewater — among the most-bought hedge-fund names of Q1 2026
signals.takeaway: The broadest large-cap AI conviction across the entire super-investor cohort — Buffett/Abel's marquee new-money buy anchors it. Not a portfolio holding, but the cleanest read that quality-AI at a 'reasonable' multiple is where the smart money concentrated; watch the 14 Aug Q2 13Fs for whether the build continued.

signals.name: Taiwan Semiconductor
signals.label: Cleanest multi-investor + congress overlap — Tepper/Soros/Tiger/Bridgewater added, Rep. Fields bought
signals.detail: TSM added by Tepper (+17%), Soros (+49.3%), Tiger Global and Bridgewater in Q1; Rep. Cleo Fields bought 10 Jul — among the most-owned Q1 names
signals.takeaway: The picks-and-shovels AI-foundry bet with the broadest fund + congress overlap, and a positive read-through to the SMIC (0981) sympathy leg of the HK book. The AWS-capex re-validation ($720-745bn hyperscaler 2026 guide) underpins the foundry demand thesis.

signals.name: Nvidia
signals.label: Crowded but contested — added by Soros/Tiger/Bridgewater, trimmed by Druckenmiller and congress; Burry's legacy short
signals.detail: Q1: Soros +61.2%, Tiger and Bridgewater added; Druckenmiller trimmed -7%; congress (Liccardo 21 Jul, Meuser Jun) selling; Burry's Q3-2025 NVDA put still on. WSB top-mention
signals.takeaway: The market's most crowded long with visible profit-taking (funds and congress both trimming into strength) and a marquee bear (Burry) — a two-sided, high-beta bellwether. Its round-trip (>$1trn drawdown then record snapback) is the cleanest gauge of AI-complex risk appetite for the SMIC chip leg.

signals.name: Micron
signals.label: Memory upcycle — Tepper's #2 holding, added by Bridgewater; Burry short the other side
signals.detail: MU is ~9.5% of Appaloosa (Tepper's #2), added by Bridgewater in Q1; Burry reportedly added to a Micron short 24 Jul; active/mixed on WSB
signals.takeaway: The AI-memory play with heavyweight fund conviction (Tepper) against a marquee short (Burry) — a high-beta battleground leveraged to the AI-hardware capex cycle and a read on the broader semis/HK-chip sentiment.

signals.name: Energy Fuels
signals.label: Insider-validated + dated catalyst — CEO/dir open-market buys ($12.70-13.08) and a new commercial heavy-REE plant
signals.detail: CEO/dir bought ~$1.0M open-market 7-8 Jul at $12.695-13.08; UUUU began building a commercial heavy-REE plant at White Mesa on 29 Jul; 6 Aug conference call; Lynas's $96M Pentagon deal reinforces the ex-China theme
signals.takeaway: The rare-earth watchlist's cleanest confluence: genuine insider buying, a concrete Western heavy-REE catalyst, and the 10 Nov MOFCOM suspension cliff as the calendar risk. Accumulate government-backed UUUU/MP on weakness rather than chase; the 6 Aug call is the near-term tell.

signals.name: Palantir
signals.label: Bull/bear battleground — retail/momentum favorite vs Burry's large legacy put
signals.detail: WSB/momentum favorite with high short interest; Burry's Q3-2025 book held puts on ~5M PLTR shares (~$912M notional), reportedly ~+35%, though he trimmed (not covered) with PLTR ~$112-118
signals.takeaway: A sentiment-driven, high-short-interest volatility flag — the cleanest expression of the retail-momentum-vs-valuation-bear tension in the AI complex. Not a holding, but a useful barometer of speculative risk appetite.

congress.rationale: The California Democrat sold Nvidia (disclosed 29 Jul, tx 21 Jul) — trimming the AI leader into the late-July chip rout; the group has since REBOUNDED to records on AWS-capex re-validation, so the exit reads early. Part of a broad congress large-cap-tech distribution (AltIndex 30d: most-sold NVDA/MSFT/GOOGL/AAPL).
congress.deepDive: A fresh exit from the semis leader by a member on the tech-heavy side of Congress, echoing Rep. Meuser's June NVDA partial-sale series — profit-taking after a huge run rather than a directional bet, but notable as congress net-distributes mega-cap AI even as the index makes records.

congress.rationale: The Connecticut Democrat cut Exxon — trimming energy exposure just before the 3 Aug Iran de-escalation crashed oil ~5-7%, a well-timed reduction against the crude rollover.
congress.deepDive: Himes disclosed a cluster of trims (XOM, HD, BAC) dated 20 Jul — a de-risking across energy, consumer/housing and banks that looks prescient into the oil crash and the still-hawkish rate backdrop.

congress.rationale: Reduced Home Depot — cutting a rate-sensitive consumer/housing name into the higher-for-longer backdrop (10Y ~4.7%).
congress.deepDive: Part of Himes's 20 Jul de-risking cluster; trimming housing-linked consumer exposure is consistent with caution on the rate-sensitive consumer even as equities rallied to records.

congress.rationale: Trimmed Bank of America — lightening bank exposure alongside the XOM/HD sells in a broad 20 Jul de-risking.
congress.deepDive: A small bank trim within the cluster; banks have been resilient on NIMs but Himes reduced across the board rather than a single-name view.

congress.rationale: The Michigan Democrat bought Freddie Mac — a GSE-privatization angle bet, one of the few congress BUYS in a period of large-cap-tech distribution.
congress.deepDive: GSE (Fannie/Freddie) names have drawn periodic congressional interest tied to privatization/conservatorship-exit headlines; a fresh buy is a speculative policy-catalyst play distinct from the mega-cap complex.

congress.rationale: The Louisiana Democrat bought Taiwan Semiconductor — a foundry/AI-semis conviction buy that overlaps with heavy super-investor accumulation (Tepper, Soros, Tiger, Bridgewater all added TSM in Q1).
congress.deepDive: TSM is the cleanest multi-investor + congress overlap this run — the picks-and-shovels AI-foundry bet — and a positive read-through to the SMIC (0981) sympathy leg of the HK book.

congress.rationale: The Washington Democrat bought Amphenol — an AI-connector/datacenter-hardware demand play, part of a 8 Jul basket rotation.
congress.deepDive: Amphenol is a levered play on AI-datacenter buildout (connectors/interconnects); the buy sits inside Larsen's 8 Jul rotation that also added MCK while trimming SPGI/ABT.

congress.rationale: Bought McKesson — a defensive healthcare-distribution add within Larsen's 8 Jul basket.
congress.deepDive: Healthcare distribution is a low-beta defensive; pairing an AI-hardware buy (APH) with a defensive (MCK) is a barbell rotation.

congress.rationale: Sold S&P Global — rotating out of ratings/data within the 8 Jul basket reshuffle.
congress.deepDive: Trimming a richly-valued data/ratings compounder to fund the AI-hardware/defensive adds; a valuation-rotation tell rather than a sector call.

congress.rationale: Trimmed Abbott Laboratories — lightening med-devices in the 8 Jul rotation.
congress.deepDive: Part of the same basket reshuffle; funds the APH/MCK adds.

congress.rationale: The Nevada Democrat sold Full House Resorts — a local NV gaming name, a small-cap trim.
congress.deepDive: A home-state small-cap disposal; idiosyncratic rather than a macro signal, but useful color on the breadth of congress trading beyond mega-caps.

congress.rationale: The New Jersey Republican sold Analog Devices — a semis profit-take after the group's run, one of the few GOP disclosures in the sample.
congress.deepDive: Analog/industrial-semis trim; consistent with the broader congress pattern of distributing semiconductor winners into strength.

congress.rationale: The California Democrat trimmed a regional bank (RBC Bearings/Regional) position — a small 30 Jun disposal.
congress.deepDive: A minor regional trim; adds to the picture of congress lightening cyclicals/financials at the margin.

congress.rationale: The Pennsylvania Republican disclosed a series of NVIDIA partial disposals (~mid-June) — steady profit-taking in the AI leader, presaging Liccardo's later NVDA sale.
congress.deepDive: A multi-lot sell program rather than a single exit; together with Liccardo's July sale it captures the bipartisan congressional trimming of NVDA into strength even as institutions stay long.

superInvestors.name: Berkshire Hathaway / Warren Buffett
superInvestors.rationale: Berkshire nearly tripled Alphabet to ~57.8M shares (~$16.6B) while fully EXITING Visa, Mastercard, UnitedHealth and Amazon and cutting Chevron ~35% — a decisive quality-AI tilt under Abel with cash near a record ~$397B.
superInvestors.deepDive: The marquee Q1 move: a giant new-money Alphabet stake funded by exiting payments/health and trimming energy signals a concentrated quality-compounder pivot. GOOGL is now the broadest large-cap AI conviction across the whole 13F universe (also held by Soros, Tepper, Tiger, Bridgewater). Q2 13F due 14 Aug will show whether the build continued.

superInvestors.name: Soros Fund Management
superInvestors.rationale: Soros added NVDA (+61.2%), TSM (+49.3%) and AAPL (+20.3%), opened a new EA stake (+$109M) and a small new BRK-B — an AI-semis tilt on top of AMZN/EA/NVDA/TSM/GOOGL as top holdings.
superInvestors.deepDive: The fund leaned INTO AI semis in Q1 (NVDA/TSM adds) — the opposite of its prior-quarter S&P 500 index-put hedge, which had looked prescient on the 29 Jul drop before the record snapback trimmed the edge. A net risk-on posture into the AI complex.

superInvestors.name: Gates Foundation Trust
superInvestors.rationale: The Gates Foundation Trust sold its last ~$3.2B of Microsoft, completing a two-decade wind-down of the founder stake; the ~$31.7B/22-holding portfolio is now anchored by BRK-B, WM, Canadian National, Caterpillar and Deere with no new positions.
superInvestors.deepDive: A structural, non-signal exit (endowment diversification, not a view on MSFT) — but it removes a long-standing anchor holder. The remaining book skews defensive/industrial (rails, waste, machinery), a conservative posture.

superInvestors.name: Duquesne / Stanley Druckenmiller
superInvestors.rationale: Druckenmiller trimmed NVDA (-7%), added MSFT (+22%) and rotated into Broadcom (AVGO) — even building and exiting a GOOGL position within the same quarter. Top-5: NVDA, Coupang, MSFT, Eli Lilly, Teck.
superInvestors.deepDive: Characteristic high-turnover rotation: shaving the crowded NVDA long while leaning into AVGO and MSFT as the preferred AI-infra vehicles, with a GLP-1 (LLY) and materials (TECK) barbell.

superInvestors.name: Pershing Square / Bill Ackman
superInvestors.rationale: Ackman added ~1.84M Amazon shares (moving it to his #2 position, ~$2.4B), pushed a new ~$2.1-2.4B Microsoft stake into the top-4 (funded by slashing Alphabet ~95%), and EXITED Hilton. Four un-named new Q2 positions are teased for the 14 Aug report.
superInvestors.deepDive: The MSFT build looks well-timed into Microsoft's ~15% 30 Jul gain, and the AMZN add was vindicated by the AWS blowout. A concentrated mega-cap-AI tilt; the four teased Q2 names plus the Pershing Square USA IPO are the awaited catalysts.

superInvestors.name: Bridgewater / Ray Dalio
superInvestors.rationale: Bridgewater added the chip complex (NVDA, AVGO, MU, TSM) while exiting/reducing software (CRM, NOW, WDAY, ADBE) across its ~$22.4B/993-holding book; top positions SPY, IVV, AMZN, NVDA, GOOGL.
superInvestors.deepDive: A systematic hardware-over-software rotation within tech — leaning into the AI-semis capex cycle and out of application software, consistent with the hyperscaler-capex re-acceleration ($720-745bn 2026 guide).

superInvestors.name: Appaloosa / David Tepper
superInvestors.rationale: Tepper added AMZN (+98%), UBER (+242%), VST (+114%) and TSM (+17%), opened a new SanDisk (SNDK) stake, and REDUCED BABA/META/MSFT while exiting the airlines and FXI — top-5 AMZN, MU, GOOGL, UBER, TSM.
superInvestors.deepDive: Tepper kept his structural 'buy China' tilt (BABA still a top holding, KWEB added earlier) but trimmed it into strength while leaning harder into US AI/power (VST) and consumer-internet (AMZN, UBER). Micron (MU) remains a large ~9.5% memory-upcycle bet.

superInvestors.name: Tiger Global / Chase Coleman
superInvestors.rationale: Tiger Global added NVDA, TSM, META, AVGO, Spotify, Coupang and AMAT (plus a new ~$72M Intel stake earlier), reduced AMZN/MSFT and exited Flutter/Veeva/Grab/Workday; top-5 GOOGL/NVDA/AMZN/TSM/META (~48%).
superInvestors.deepDive: A concentrated mega-cap-AI + semi-cap-equipment (AMAT) tilt; the top-5 at ~48% of the book underscores the crowding into the same handful of AI winners across the whole super-investor cohort.

superInvestors.name: Trump Media & Technology (DJT)
superInvestors.rationale: Trump Media's crypto-treasury held ~9,542 BTC (~$647M) and 756.1M CRO (~$53M) at 31 Mar, driving a ~$406M Q1 net loss on crypto markdowns — tying DJT's equity to crypto beta.
superInvestors.deepDive: The treasury strategy makes DJT a levered crypto proxy; with BTC soft (~$62-63k) and lagging the equity records, the crypto-treasury build has been a drag into month-end rather than a tailwind. A reported (unverified) Trump PLTR add is not 13F-confirmed.

superInvestors.name: Scion / Michael Burry (personal)
superInvestors.rationale: Having wound down Scion (final Q4 2025 13F) and now publishing on Substack, Burry trades personally — his headline AI shorts date to the Q3 2025 13F (puts on ~5M PLTR/~$912M notional and ~1M NVDA/~$187M notional, ~80% of the book) and he reportedly ADDED to a Micron short on 24 Jul. The per-share short prices were not verifiable this run and are omitted.
superInvestors.deepDive: The marquee AI bear: the PLTR put reportedly sits ~+35% while the NVDA put ($110 strike, Dec-2027) is still underwater after the chip rebound. Not 13F-reportable (personal/newsletter) and sizes unconfirmed — treated as a sentiment flag, not a position figure, with no fabricated prices.

insiders.rationale: Tencent ran near-daily buybacks through early July under its 10% AGM mandate, then SUSPENDED the program into the customary blackout ahead of its 12 August interim results — the buyback remains dark into that print. Values read from HKEX next-day filings; no per-share price asserted.
insiders.deepDive: Tencent's repurchase is a near-mechanical corporate bid that underpinned the stock through the HK-tech rebound; the blackout removes that prop right as the Hang Seng makes its best week since Sep-2025 and into the 12 Aug results. Internet sleeve stays favored over the SMIC chip leg; watch for the buyback to resume post-results.

insiders.rationale: Xiaomi repurchased 3.9M Class B shares for HK$100.7M on 15 July 2026 (HKEX next-day filing) — continuing its buyback alongside the EV-delivery momentum that drove the +7.7% pop on the new 'Sky Nomad' models, a company backing its own equity while Tencent's buyback goes dark. Shares and total value read from the filing; no per-share price asserted.
insiders.deepDive: With Tencent in blackout, Xiaomi's continuing bid is a relative support within the internet sleeve. Xiaomi remains a high-beta HK-tech name with EV optionality that offers catch-up if the rally broadens on Politburo follow-through.

insiders.insider: Ross R. Bhappu (CEO) & Bruce D. Hansen (Director)
insiders.rationale: Open-market cluster buying by Energy Fuels' top brass: CEO Bhappu bought 74,000 shares at $13.08 on 7 Jul and director Hansen 4,000 at $12.695 on 8 Jul; both Form 4s accepted by SEC EDGAR 9 Jul (prices read from the filings). Lands with UUUU's 29 Jul heavy-REE-plant catalyst and its 6 Aug call.
insiders.deepDive: Rare genuine open-market buys (not option exercises) in the portfolio's uranium/rare-earth name — management conviction at the $12.70-13.08 zone makes that band an insider-validated reference. Still the only confirmed insider BUYING across the portfolio's mining names, against heavy AI-complex insider selling elsewhere.

insiders.role: EVP & Chief Sustainability and Development Officer
insiders.rationale: Newmont's EVP sold 3,000 shares (~$277K) at $92.38 on 1 July 2026 under a Rule 10b5-1 plan dated 17 Dec 2025, leaving 43,315 shares — routine pre-scheduled selling at the world's largest gold miner (a top GDX holding); price read from the Form 4.
insiders.deepDive: A scheduled 10b5-1 disposal, so the signal is muted. As the largest US-filing gold producer and a core GDX constituent, Newmont insider activity reads on miner sentiment; the absence of open-market buying is consistent with a sector that already re-rated hard. Most GDX/SILJ miners are Canadian and report on SEDI.

insiders.rationale: DBS CEO Tan Su Shan sold 100,000 shares at S$60.12 on 15 May 2026, leaving ~1.3M shares (0.048% of the bank) — a partial profit-take and the most recent verified insider move on the SGX-listed bank (latest available).
insiders.deepDive: DBS has since pushed to fresh records into its 6 August results; the sale is a liquidity/diversification trim rather than lost confidence given Tan's retained stake. No within-window director/substantial-shareholder change was verifiable for DBS this run; DBS continues a S$3bn buyback through 2027.

insiders.value: ~5.1% of Singtel; average ~S$4.67/share over the accumulation window
insiders.rationale: Capital Group crossed above the 5% substantial-shareholder threshold in Singtel (triggering tx 6 May, SGX filing lodged 8 May 2026), reporting 837,947,249 shares (5.1%) bought at an AVERAGE ~S$4.67 over the accumulation period — likely the second-largest holder after Temasek. This is the latest available substantial-shareholder filing for Singtel; date CORRECTED from the prior file (was mis-stated as 13 Jul).
insiders.deepDive: A global institution crossing 5% is a meaningful vote of confidence in Singtel's capital-return/asset-recycling story (and its own S$2B Value Realisation buyback). The S$4.67 is explicitly an accumulation-window AVERAGE per the source — NOT a single-day execution price.
